slides.title: Uni-VLaT: Whole-Body Tactile Adaptation of VLA Policies for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.tldr: WHOLE-BODY TACTILE INTEGRATION FOR VLA POLICIES
slides.highlight: Uni-VLaT integrates distributed tactile sensing into vision-language-action policies to improve humanoid loco-manipulation and human-robot contact. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Uni-VLaT adapts pretrained VLA policies for humanoid loco-manipulation using whole-body tactile sensing and predictive supervision.
card.key_idea: Integrates distributed tactile tokens into a VLA policy and uses a tactile-anchored multimodal context to predict future tactile, proprioceptive, and visual latent representations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-robot tasks using Unitree G1; achieved 75% average success rate, outperforming non-tactile baselines by 43 points.
card.limitation: Sensors are sensitive to noise and mounting variation; limited whole-body tactile simulation restricts large-scale robustness studies.

slides.title: Unified Visual-Tactile-Action Modeling from Human Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: SCALABLE HUMAN TACTILE DATA FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: A Unified Visual-Tactile-Action Model leverages human tactile demonstrations to improve robot control in contact-rich tasks, achieving a 70% average success rate.

card.one_liner: UVTA leverages scalable human tactile demonstrations to improve contact-aware dexterous robot manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: A unified model maps human and robot data into aligned tactile-action representations, jointly predicting future actions and tactile trajectories to learn shared interaction physics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five contact-rich tasks using real robots; achieved 70% average success rate, significantly outperforming T-Rex (29%) and other visuo-tactile baselines.
card.limitation: Human trajectories are not directly executable by robots, requiring combined robot-specific action supervision for successful deployment.

slides.title: TacGooseBumps (TacGB): Retrofitting Normal-Only Tactile Sensors with Shear Encoding for Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: MECHANICAL SHEAR ENCODING FOR TACTILE SENSORS
slides.highlight: TacGooseBumps introduces a passive domed film that encodes tangential loading into pressure maps, allowing policies to distinguish contact states without calibrated shear measurements. This approach improves success rates and efficiency in contact-rich manipulation tasks like insertion and fragile-object placement.

card.one_liner: TacGB retrofits normal-only tactile sensors with passive domes to encode shear for improved robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: A passive elastomeric dome array converts tangential loading into spatial pressure redistributions, allowing end-to-end policies to distinguish shear-dependent states without metric force calibration or new electronics.
card.evaluation: Tested on USB/lightbulb insertion, egg transfer, and drawing using imitation learning. Success rates increased up to 36 percentage points; contact quality improved.
card.limitation: Signal magnitude depends on dome geometry and material; changing interfaces may require collecting new policy training data.

slides.title: DexTaG: Tactile-as-Guidance in Reinforcement Learning for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: DexTaG uses glove-based tactile signals to guide reinforcement learning toward human contact patterns, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural skill and aligning human-AI intent in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: DexTaG uses glove-captured tactile signals to guide RL for natural, contact-rich dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Tactile-as-Guidance rewards (fingertip proximity and map similarity) guide a generalizable retargeter, which is then distilled into a tactile-free student controller for real-world deployment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on marker-pen, hammer, and OakInk2 tasks. DexTaG outperformed distance-based baselines in trajectory completion and grasp naturalness (user study).
card.limitation: Real-world grasp acquisition is a bottleneck, with high failure rates attributed to initial object placement offsets.

slides.title: Gaze Prompts: Temporally Dense Human Attention for Vision-Language-Action Fine-Tuning
slides.highlight: This work uses eye-tracker-supervised gaze prompting to provide frame-level visual guidance for robot manipulation, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and attention modeling.

card.one_liner: Gaze Prompts improve VLA fine-tuning by using human gaze as temporally dense visual guidance.
card.key_idea: Human gaze from VR teleoperation is rendered as crosshairs during training; a lightweight predictor estimates these gaze locations at deployment to provide visual prompts without eye-trackers.
card.evaluation: Tested on six real-world bimanual tasks using $\pi_0$; mean success increased from 26.3% to 56.0% compared to vanilla fine-tuning.
card.limitation: Performance depends on gaze prediction accuracy; generalization to unseen instructions, novel tasks, or different robot embodiments is not yet established.

slides.title: mmHRI: Towards Privacy-Preserving Human-Robot Interaction with Millimeter-Wave Radar
slides.highlight: This work introduces mmHRI, a framework using millimeter-wave radar to enable robot interaction and action recognition without relying on RGB cameras. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction by providing a method for privacy-preserving sensing in sensitive environments.

card.one_liner: mmHRI enables privacy-preserving robot interaction by using mmWave radar to sense human intent through occlusions.
card.key_idea: A dual-stream architecture fusing raw radar tensors and point clouds, enhanced by a memory state-space model (MSSM) to estimate human actions and 3D poses for VLA control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a custom radar dataset and real-robot trials; achieved 85.09% action-recognition accuracy under occlusion, outperforming existing radar-based baselines.
card.limitation: Cannot handle multiple subjects, perform radar-only grasping, or physically interact with curtains.

slides.title: Principal Steering Subspaces for Online Adaptation of Frozen Generative Robot Policies
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT ONLINE ADAPTATION OF FROZEN GENERATIVE ROBOT POLICIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces Principal Steering Subspaces (PSS) to enable faster and more stable online adaptation of frozen generative policies, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

card.one_liner: PSS enables efficient online adaptation of frozen generative robot policies by controlling a low-dimensional response-ranked latent subspace.
card.key_idea: Uses finite-difference probes to identify the most influential latent directions (Principal Steering Subspaces) for SAC to control, while resampling the remaining orthogonal complement from the Gaussian prior.
card.evaluation: Tested on three RoboMimic tasks (diffusion/flow-matching) and a humanoid VLA. PSS showed faster convergence and higher final success rates than full-latent control.
card.limitation: Simulation used only one seed per condition; real-robot study was exploratory with small sample size (10 trials) and no full-latent baseline.

slides.title: DexRoam: Learning Mobile Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Whole-Body Human Demonstrations
slides.tldr: LEARNING MOBILE BIMANUAL DEXTERITY FROM EGOCENTRIC HUMAN DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a system for mapping egocentric whole-body human demonstrations to robot action spaces, supporting the MOSAIC goal of using ego-exo views to improve skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: DexRoam enables mobile bimanual dexterous manipulation by transferring continuous, coupled human demonstrations to robots.
card.key_idea: A tracker-free capture system and a three-stage alignment process (embodiment, action-semantic, and temporal) map human motions into a robot-compatible, relative action space for VLA policy learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks using GR00T N1.7 and π0.5; success rates increased from 29% to 56% (GR00T) and 32% to 57% (π0.5).
card.limitation: Human data cannot replace robot data entirely; robot demonstrations remain necessary to ground the policy in the target embodiment.
